arxiv-1708-07782.title: James’ Submodule Theorem and the Steinberg Module This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on the Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups and Related Topics. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/symmetric-groups-2018.html
arxiv-1708-07782.creator: Meinolf GECK
arxiv-1708-07782.description: Abstract James’ submodule theorem is a fundamental result in the representation theory of the symmetric groups and the finite general linear groups. In this note we consider a version of that theorem for a general finite group with a split B ​ N BN -pair.

arxiv-2209-13104.title: A neural network approach for stochastic optimal control Thanks: Submitted to the editors March 10, 2023.
arxiv-2209-13104.creator: Xingjian Li, Deepanshu Verma, Lars Ruthotto
arxiv-2209-13104.description: Abstract We present a neural network approach for approximating the value function of high-dimensional stochastic control problems. Our training process simultaneously updates our value function estimate and identifies the part of the state space likely to be visited by optimal trajectories.

arxiv-2211-06718.title: Philosophical Foundations of Loop Quantum Gravity
arxiv-2211-06718.creator: Carlo Rovelli and Francesca Vidotto
arxiv-2211-06718.description: Abstract Understanding the quantum aspects of gravity is not only a matter of equations and experiments. Gravity is intimately connected with the structure of space and time, and understanding quantum gravity requires us to find a conceptual structure appropriate to make sense of the quantum aspects of space and time.

arxiv-2308-13401.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Carla Binucci, Aaron Büngener, Giuseppe Di Battista, Walter Didimo, Vida Dujmović, Seok-Hee Hong, Michael Kaufmann, Giuseppe Liotta, Pat Morin, Alessandra Tappini. pmc-10621823.creator: Lu Liu, Bo Yu, Lingxian Xu, Shiyi Wang, Lingzhi Zhao, Huang Wu
pmc-10621823.description: PurposeStereopsis is the ability to perceive depth using the slightly different views from two eyes. pmc-12773322.description: IntroductionCerebrovascular disease (CVD), particularly carotid artery atherosclerosis, contributes substantially to global morbidity and mortality. The ability to precisely detect atherosclerosis is crucial, as it directly influences patient management, including decisions regarding surgical interventions. Given the high prevalence and severe outcomes of CVD, there is an urgent need for improved early detection methods.
